scenario: An agricultural research station compares two fertilizers (A and B) for wheat yield. Fertilizer A was mostly applied to sandy soil (easy to grow), while B was mostly applied to clay soil (harder to grow). The station's report recommends Fertilizer A based on overall average yield.

data.description: Wheat yield (tonnes/hectare) by soil type and fertilizer.

question: The report recommends Fertilizer A (4.40 t/ha overall vs B's 3.10 t/ha). (a) Which fertilizer yields more on sandy soil? (b) Which fertilizer yields more on clay soil? (c) If a new farm has equal areas of sandy and clay soil (50/50), which fertilizer maximises expected yield? Compute both corrected yields.

ground_truth.explanation: B outperforms A on both soil types (+0.5 t/ha each). The aggregate reversal occurs because A was deployed on 80% sandy soil (high yield) while B was deployed on 80% clay soil (low yield). Corrected for equal mix: B=4.00 > A=3.50.

naive_answer: Fertilizer A, because 4.40 t/ha > 3.10 t/ha overall.
naive_trap: A classic Simpson's reversal. A was almost entirely used on the easier sandy soil. B was almost entirely used on the harder clay soil. Comparing aggregate yields ignores this soil-type confounding entirely.
